 J U D G M E N T

The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Yeshwanthpur Sub-Division, Bangalore City, has submitted charge sheet against the accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offence punishable U/s.498A and 304-B r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act in Crime No.623/2018 of Peenya P.S.
2.

entities.text: Dowry Prohibition Act in Crime No.623/2018

sentences.text:
The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The marriage of accused No.1 with deceased Smt.Savithri was performed on 24.11.2017 at Kalaburgi.
At the time of marriage, on demand of accused persons given dowry of Rs.1 lakh and two thola gold articles by the parents of the deceased.

After marriage, the accused persons and deceased started to reside at Nelagadaranahalli,
Nagasandra Post, Bengaluru-73, after sometime accused persons with common intention subjected the deceased to mental and physical torture demanding additional dowry of Rs.15 lakhs.

Due to the continuous torture of the accused persons, the deceased unable to tolerate and driven her to commit suicide by hanging herself at her matrimonial house on 10.12.2018 at 6.05 p.m and thereby the accused persons have committed the alleged offences as alleged against them.

3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the jurisdictional XLV Addl., CMM.,
Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused persons.

The same was numbered as SC No.1552/2019.
4.
The charge has framed against the accused persons for the offences as alleged against them.
The accused persons pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5. The prosecution has examined thirteen witnesses as PW.1 to PW.13 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P23.
On consent of accused counsel, Death Intimation, Post Mortem report, requisition of IO, UDR FIR, complaint, UDR Mahazar have marked at Ex.P.14 to 17 respectively.
As such the learned PP has gave up the witnesses CWs.12, 13, 15 to 21.

This court has been issued summons, warrant and proclamation against C.W.8, 10, 11, since the concerned police unexecuted the warrant and keeping the said witnesses present before the court,
hence the prayer of the learned public prosecutor was rejected and the said witnesses CWs.8, 10 and 11 were dropped.
The learned PP has gave up C.W.22 in view of evidence of C.W.24/P.W.12.
The prosecution side evidence has completed on 18.08.2025.

sentences.text: After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused persons, as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused persons have denied incriminating evidence present against them and not chosen to lead defense evidence nor submitted anything to Court.
The accused persons have complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bonds and surety bonds.

7. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
8.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 married the deceased Smt.Savithri on 24.11.2017 at Kalburgi, and at the time of marriage accused No.1 being the husband and accused Nos.2 and 3 are being the parents-in-law of the deceased Smt.Savithri on demand received cash of Rs.1,00,000/- and gold articles as dowry from the parents of deceased and thereby the accused Nos.1 to 3 have committed the offence punishable under Sec.3 of the Dowry Prohibition Act?
2. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 being husband and accused Nos.2 and 3 being the parents-in-law of deceased Smt.Savithri and after the marriage, when the deceased started to reside alongwith accused Nos.1 to 3 at Neladaranahalli within the limits of Peenya P.S, Bengaluru, accused Nos.1 to 3 with common intnetion subjected her to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry in terms of Rs.15,00,000/- and thereby the accused Nos.1 to 3 have committed the offence punishable under Sec.4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act?
3. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused Nos.2 and 3 are being parents-in- law of deceased Smt.Savithri, and after marriage, when the deceased started to reside alongwith accused Nos.1 to 3 at Neladaranahalli within the limits of Peenya PS., Bengaluru, accused Nos.1 to 3 with common intention subjected her to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry of Rs.15,00,000/- and thereby the accused Nos.1 and 2 have committed the offence punishable under Sec.498A r/w.sec.34 of IPC?
4. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 being husband and accused Nos.2 and 3 being the parents-in-law of deceased Smt.Savithri and after marriage when the deceased started to reside alongwith accused Nos.1 to 3 at Neladaranahalli within the limits of Peenya PS., Bengaluru,
accused Nos.1 to 3 with common intention subjected her to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry in terms of Rs.15,00,000/- unable to tolerate the torture of accused Nos.1 to 3 deceased Smt.Savithri had committed suicide by hanging herself on 10.12.2018 at 6.05 p.m at her matrimonial house and such cruelty and harassment as did drive the said deceased Smt.Savithri to commit suicide within 7 years of marriage by hanging herself and accused No.1 being her husband and accused Nos.2 and 3 being the parents-in-law of the deceased Smt.Savithri,
subjected her to cruelty and harassment in connection with the demand for additional dowry and thereby the accused persons have committed the offence punishable under Section 304B r/w.34 of Peenya Ps vs A1 - Mahesh Subhash Savalagi on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97490530/
3 of IPC?
5.
What order?

9. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: In the Negative  Point No.5: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 10.
Points No.1 to 4: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.

The prosecution has examined the parents and sister of the deceased as PWs.1, 2 and 4, the younger aunt of the deceased as P.W.3, the villagers of PWs.1 to 4 as PWs.5 to 7, the neighbours of the deceased's matrimonial house as P.W.8 and the police official witnesses as PWs.9, 10, 12 and 13 to establish the guilt against the accused persons.

On perusal of the prosecution papers and also evidence of PWs.1 to 8, 11 clearly goes to show that the marriage between the deceased and accused No.1 was performed on 24.11.2017 according to their customs at Sai Mandira Kalyana Mantapa situated behind Sarvagna college, at Kalburgi.
After marriage, they started their marital life alongwith accused Nos.2 and 3 i.e. parents of the accused No.1 at Nelagadaranahalli.
It is the allegations against the accused persons that they received Rs.1 lakh and gold ornaments as dowry at the time of marriage.
Thereafter the accused persons started to demand additional dowry of Rs.15 lakhs to the deceased Savithri.
Even after the settlement talks, the accused persons did not stopped the physical and mental harassment to the deceased for additional dowry.
As such the deceased was fed up due to the ill-treatment of the accused persons and committed suicide by hanging herself at her matrimonial home on 10.12.2018 at 6.05 p.m.

Whereas the evidence of parents, of the deceased Sri.Shivaleela, Sri.Rajashekar Sanakkar, sister of the deceased Smt.Lakshmi and younger aunt of the deceased Vimala Bai examined as PWs.1 to 4 never ever deposed regarding the cruelty received by the deceased from the accused persons, so also they never supported the prosecution deposing that the accused persons insisted the deceased to bring additional dowry from her parental house by selling the ancestral property by giving physical and mental harassment.
Since the evidence of PWs.1 to 4 goes against to the prosecution story, hence, the learned PP has treated PWs.1 to 4 as hostile to bring out supportive evidence.
Unfortunately, the learned PP has not able to get any useful evidence from the mouth of PWs.1 to 4.
So also, the mother of the deceased not supported the contents of the complaint marked at Ex.P.1 by saying that she is not aware of the contents of the complaint.

Though the prosecution has succeeded to get mark the marriage photo and invitation at Peenya Ps vs A1 - Mahesh Subhash Savalagi on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97490530/

sentences.text: , but the marriage between the deceased and accused No.1 is not in dispute.
As such, the evidence given by PWs.1 to 4 i.e. family members of the deceased not at all useful for the prosecution in any angle.

11. The villagers of the complainant by name Subhash, Sreekanth, Srishaila and Rajakumar examined as PWs.5 to 7, P.W.11 and also neighbour of the deceased by name Gangadaraiah examined as P.W.8 not given supportive evidence to believe due to the physical and mental torture given by the accused persons to bring additional dowry, the deceased has committed suicide.
According to these witnesses, the deceased and accused persons were leading happy life.
Though the prosecution has cross-examined the said witnesses PWs.5 to 8 and 11, perhaps not able to get any worthful evidence in support of the prosecution story.

So, the evidence given by all the independent witnesses not at all helpful to the prosecution in any angle.
12. It is pertinent to note that the police witness PW.12 Sanjay Ashoka Thippareddy PSI shows that after receiving further investigation from C.W.22 on 11.12.2018 immediately visited the spot and conducted spot Mahazar as per Ex.P.17 in the presence of panchas and seized the death note as per Ex.P.20.
The UDR documents marked at Ex.P.21 on the consent of accused counsel.
On 12.12.2018 submitted requisition as per Ex.P.22 to the witness C.W.19 to conduct inquest Mahazar.

After conducting inquest Mahazar, P.M. was carried out on the dead body of the deceased and thereafter handed over the dead body to its relatives and collected the endorsement by the police staff deputed for the said purpose.
On the same day, again C.W.1 came to the police station, lodged complaint before the C.W.22.
On the basis of said complaint, the witness C.W.22 registered FIR 623/2018 and submitted the same to the court and its copy to its superior officers.
The said FIR marked at Ex.P.23.
However the said police witness has admitted that in the death note, it has specifically written that nobody is responsible for the death of the deceased.
The witness P.W.13 Mr.Raviprasad after receiving the further investigation has visited spot, recorded statement of the witnesses and collected inquest report and also marriage photos and invitation.

Since not received the FSL.Report,
hence he has deputed C.W.23 to bring the hand written answer sheets pertaining to the deceased from the school, where she studied.

Accordingly the witness P.W.9 Rangaramegowda went to the Chennamalleshwara High School, studied by the deceased and collected the answer sheet from the Head Master and same was seized under Mahazar in the presence of the villagers as per Ex.P.10 and thereafter returned to the police station and handed over the same to the Investigation Officer.
The said Investigation Officer P.W.13 after collecting the same conducted Mahazar as per Ex.P.18 and brought into PF.
Thereafter he has handed over further investigation to the witness P.W.10 J.Mohan.
The said witness P.W.10 has instructed police staff to trace the accused persons.
On 09.05.2019 the accused No.1 was brought before him by the police staff.
He has arrested the accused No.1 and after the medical examination produced him before court alongwith remand application through police escort.
Later as investigation was completed, hence submitted charge sheet against the accused persons.
The evidence given by police witnesses completely denied by the advocate for accused persons.
As already discussed supra, the PSI who has seized the death note has admitted that in Ex.P.20, the deceased has written that nobody is responsible for her death.

Inspite of that the concerned police submitted charge sheet though the reasons for death may be any other reason instead of ill-treatment or harassment alleged to be given by the accused persons by demanding additional dowry.

It is very clear from the above discussions that the prosecution has utterly failed Peenya Ps vs A1 - Mahesh Subhash Savalagi on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97490530/

As such, this court has answered the point Nos.1 to 4 in the Negative.

13. Point No.5: In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 4, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused Nos.1 to 3 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304-B r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of accused Nos.1 to 3 stands cancelled.
